texts.orig: The current  study examined central assumption of the IPTS regarding the prediction of future suicide attempts in high-risk sample of adults admitted to psychiatric hospital because of suicide attempt or severe suicidal ideation within 12 months after the initial assessment. The primary finding was that, contrary to expectation, the interaction between thwarted belongingness; per ceived burdensomeness and capability for suicide did not predict suicide attempt in the 12-month follow-up-period. Although unex and contrary to the theoretical assumptions; this finding is consistent with retrospective studies in in-patient populations ' 40,41 as well as two prospective studies in adolescent populations;,11,18 neither of which found support for this main assumption of the IPTS. To our knowledge; Joiner et al'0 conducted the only study that found the three-way interaction to be predictive of suicide attempts in an in-patient sample.
